solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Butter spinach rolls diner with wife ordered

definitions.note: noun sense, flattery; the answer is the verbal noun of sawder, to flatter

indicators.note: something ordered has been put into a fresh sequence, so these letters are rearranged
to roll something is to wrap it up, so the first word encloses what follows

blocks.note: sag (saag) is spinach in Indian cookery
W is the abbreviation for wife
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A cook rolls spinach and butter for a diner and his wife who have placed an order.
explanation.walkthrough: Sag (saag) is the Indian word for spinach. 'Butter' is not the dairy spread but flattery, as in buttering someone up.
explanation.definitionFit: Sawder is soft flattery, an old word for blarney, so sawdering is flattering talk, like butter in its sense of smooth praise.

clue.text: Time right for second tenor in Italian musical group

indicators.note: one thing 'for' another means it stands in that place instead, so a letter is swapped out

blocks.note: the Italian word for a group of four players
R is the abbreviation for right
T is tenor; the second T of the Italian word is the one replaced

explanation.surface: A second tenor is right for an Italian vocal group, says a talent scout.
explanation.walkthrough: In QUARTETTO the second T becomes R. 'Second tenor' reads as a voice part, but here it picks the second letter T in the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Quarter to is a clock time, fifteen minutes before the hour, as in quarter to six.

clue.text: Bear up in Christmas rush

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of the following words
in a down clue, up means the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: the end of Christmas and the start of rush

explanation.surface: A bear in a department store gets caught up in the Christmas shopping rush.
explanation.walkthrough: ASRU sits across the two words and is read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Ursa is Latin for a she-bear, familiar from the constellations Ursa Major and Ursa Minor.

clue.text: Making no sense, police invade Swiss resort abruptly

indicators.note: cut off abruptly means the word stops short of its last letter
invaders get inside a place, so these letters go within the other word

blocks.note: Verbier, the Swiss ski resort, losing its last letter
CID, the Criminal Investigation Department of the British police

explanation.surface: Detectives make a sudden raid on a Swiss ski resort, which seems to make no sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making no sense' looks like a comment on the raid, but it is the definition, a noun phrase for destroying a word's sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Verbicide is the killing of a word's meaning by distortion, the act of making a word mean nothing.

clue.text: Labour got in after very short polling process

indicators.note: short here means the word is cut down to its first letter
to labour is to work, and these letters are worked into a new arrangement
after places the rearranged letters behind the abbreviation rather than in clue order

blocks.note: only the first letter of very
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: The Labour Party got in after a very short election campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' looks like the political party, but it signals the rearranging; 'after' puts the shuffled letters behind V.
explanation.definitionFit: Voting is the act of casting ballots, which is exactly what a poll consists of.

clue.text: Study again Knight and Queen put up to restrict King

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means the letters are raised to read bottom to top
restricting something means hemming it in, so these letters go round the other word

blocks.note: N is the chess notation for knight
ER, Elizabeth Regina
Shakespeare's King Lear

explanation.surface: A chess player studies again how knight and queen were moved up to trap the king.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess picture misleads: only the knight is chess notation; the king is Shakespeare's tragic monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: To relearn is to learn something a second time, which is studying it again.

clue.text: Designs concentrated for an audience

indicators.note: what is meant for an audience is heard rather than read

blocks.note: intense means concentrated, as in intense effort

explanation.surface: A theatre designer's work has been concentrated to suit an audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Designs' reads as stage sets; it is the definition in its sense of purposes.
explanation.definitionFit: Intents are aims or purposes, the same as designs in the sense of plans one has in mind.

clue.text: Cover for the head, dead chilly in Aberdeen

blocks.note: a caul is the membrane sometimes covering a newborn's head, also a close-fitting cap
D is the abbreviation for dead

explanation.surface: Someone in Aberdeen wants a hat because it is dead cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In Aberdeen' signals a Scots word: Aberdeen is a Scottish city.
explanation.definitionFit: Cauld is the Scots form of cold, so it means chilly as spoken in Scotland.

clue.text: Penalties in Ireland as before leading to uncertainty

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so the first word goes within the second

blocks.note: IFS, the Irish Free State, the former name of the Irish state
fines are money penalties

explanation.surface: Penalties in Ireland, as in earlier days, lead to uncertainty about the law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ireland as before' means Ireland under a former name: the Irish Free State, 1922 to 1937.
explanation.definitionFit: Iffiness is the quality of being iffy, doubtful or not certain, so it is uncertainty.

clue.text: Money lost in protest for God

indicators.note: what is lost is no longer there, so that letter drops out of the word

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for money
a demo is a protest march

explanation.surface: Money was lost in a religious protest.
explanation.walkthrough: DEMO without M.
explanation.definitionFit: Deo is the Latin dative of Deus, meaning to or for God, as in Deo gratias.

clue.text: Rosy managed to retain energy after one hour working less hard

indicators.note: less means without, and hard is shorthand for the pencil grade letter, which drops out
working letters are put to work in a new order
retaining something means keeping hold of it inside

blocks.note: a is one
hour with its H removed, then rearranged
ran means managed, as in ran a business
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: After working an hour less hard, someone was rosy-cheeked but managed to keep their energy.
explanation.walkthrough: A + (HOUR minus H, rearranged) + RAN holding E: A-URO-R(E)AN. H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils.
explanation.definitionFit: Aurorean means of the dawn, from Aurora, goddess of daybreak, and so rosy like the morning sky.

clue.text: Some sounds like expression of relief

indicators.note: the words say outright that the answer is matched by its sound

blocks.note: phew is what you say when relieved

explanation.surface: Some people make a noise like a sigh of relief.
explanation.definitionFit: A few means a small number, the same as some, as in a few biscuits.

clue.text: Unused land available to rent looked to need backing

indicators.note: backing means going in the opposite direction, so the letters are read from the end

blocks.note: to let, as on a sign for a property for rent
saw is the past of see, so looked

explanation.surface: A plot of unused land up for rent looked as though it needed financial backing.
explanation.walkthrough: TO LET + SAW is turned back to front as a whole. 'Backing' reads as financial support but signals the turnaround.
explanation.definitionFit: A waste lot is a vacant plot of ground left unbuilt or neglected, so unused land.

clue.text: Not American, famous flying objects?

indicators.note: not means without, so those letters are removed from the word
letters sent flying scatter and land in a new order

blocks.note: AM is a short form of American
taken as written

explanation.surface: Famous sightings of flying objects, but not in America.
explanation.walkthrough: FAMOUS loses AM, and the remaining four letters are rearranged. 'Flying' does double duty, signalling the anagram and starting the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: UFOs are unidentified flying objects, the abbreviation for things seen in the sky and not explained.

clue.text: A drink, short possibly

indicators.note: short means cut off, so the last letter falls away
possibly signals one possible arrangement among many of the letters

blocks.note: taken as written, then trimmed of its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone orders a drink, perhaps a short.
explanation.walkthrough: A DRINK loses K, then is rearranged. The whole clue also defines: a drain is a small drink, and a short (a measure of spirits) is one possible example.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers gives drain as slang for a drink, especially a small one, and a short is a small measure of spirits.

clue.text: Shop, one connected with Greek island

blocks.note: a deli is a delicatessen shop
an is one

explanation.surface: A shop, one with links to a Greek island.
explanation.definitionFit: Delian means relating to Delos, the small Greek island in the Cyclades sacred to Apollo.

clue.text: End of race overlooked, supporter follows a black runner

indicators.note: something overlooked is left out, so that letter is dropped
'End of' keeps only the last letter of 'race'

blocks.note: taken as written
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
a seconder supports a motion
the final letter of race

explanation.surface: A runner in the final stage of a race is ignored while a supporter tags along behind.
explanation.walkthrough: A + B, then SECONDER with its first E dropped. 'Runner' is not an athlete but one who runs away.
explanation.definitionFit: An absconder is someone who flees secretly, typically from custody or debts, a runner in that sense.

clue.text: Note adult holiday-makers with nothing taken off — certainly not ____!

definitions.note: the blank stands for the answer: holiday-makers with nothing taken off are certainly not these, who take everything off

indicators.note: taken off means removed, so that letter is removed from the word

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for note
A is the film certificate for adult
tourists make holidays
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A notice about holiday-makers who keep their clothes on: these are certainly not nudists!
explanation.walkthrough: N + A + TOURISTS without O. The joke is that people with 'nothing taken off' are the opposite of those who strip everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Naturists are nudists, who take all their clothes off, so they are certainly not people with nothing taken off.

clue.text: Mark's repelled by terrible Russian, not Victor — Boris?

indicators.note: repelled means driven back, so the word is read backwards
not means without, so that letter is taken away

blocks.note: to note is to mark, take notice of
Ivan the Terrible, tsar of Russia
V is Victor in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A man named Mark is repelled by a dreadful Russian; is this Boris?
explanation.walkthrough: NOTE backwards + IVAN without V. Boris Johnson went to Eton, the English boarding school, so he is an example, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: An Etonian is a pupil or former pupil of Eton College, and Boris Johnson is a famous example.

clue.text: Work before one for great success briefly

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: or is an old word for before, as in or ever
a is one
to can mean for, as in the key to the door
a riot is a huge success, as in the show was a riot; trimmed of its last letter

explanation.surface: A piece of work came before one that was briefly a great success.
explanation.definitionFit: An oratorio is a large musical work for voices and orchestra, such as Handel's Messiah, and a work is a composition.

clue.text: US town cut and cut plant

indicators.note: a word that is cut loses its last letter

blocks.note: burg is American slang for a town; cut short
to dock is to cut, as with a tail or wages

explanation.surface: An American town was trimmed back and a plant was cut down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' appears twice: first as the shortening signal, then as a word meaning dock.
explanation.definitionFit: Burdock is a coarse weedy plant with hooked burrs, the dandelion-and-burdock plant.

clue.text: The most early hill fort is in France

blocks.note: a rath is an ancient Irish hill fort
est is French for is

explanation.surface: The oldest hill fort is in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The most early' reads as describing the fort, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Rathe is an old word for early, as in rathe-ripe, so its superlative rathest means earliest.

clue.text: Bill getting bogged down is regarded with respect

blocks.note: an ad is an advertisement, a bill posted up
mired means stuck in a bog

explanation.surface: Bill, despite getting stuck in a rut, is well respected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name; it is a poster.
explanation.definitionFit: To be admired is to be looked up to with approval, the same as regarded with respect.

clue.text: Easily angered aircraftsman in one list for Prestwick

indicators.note: one thing in another goes inside it

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
rund is a Scots word for a list, a strip or selvage of cloth
AC is the abbreviation for aircraftsman

explanation.surface: An irritable airman is posted onto a list at Prestwick air base.
explanation.walkthrough: Prestwick is a town in Scotland, so a Scots word is wanted. A list here is a strip of cloth such as a selvage, not a roll of names.
explanation.definitionFit: Iracund means inclined to anger, from Latin iracundus, so describes someone easily angered.

clue.text: Commercial vessels free alongside ship securing a great deal

indicators.note: securing something means holding it fast inside

blocks.note: FAS is the shipping term free alongside ship
a lot is a great deal

explanation.surface: Merchant ships are delivered free alongside a ship, and the trader secures a great deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Flotas were Spanish fleets of merchant ships sailing to and from the Americas, so commercial vessels.

clue.text: Sir Michael upset with old computer

indicators.note: upset means tipped over, so in a down clue the letters are turned upside down

blocks.note: Sir Michael Caine, the actor

explanation.surface: Sir Michael is annoyed with an outdated computer.
explanation.definitionFit: ENIAC was among the first electronic general-purpose computers, built in the 1940s, so a very old machine.

clue.text: Got up around chimney to reverse paint-making apparatus

indicators.note: one word goes around another, enclosing it
to reverse is to run backwards, so the whole is read from the end

blocks.note: rose is the past of rise
lum is a Scots and northern word for chimney

explanation.surface: A sweep got up round the chimney to reverse a paint-mixing machine.
explanation.walkthrough: Lum is a Scots word for chimney; the turnaround applies to the whole assembled word, not just one piece.
explanation.definitionFit: An emulsor is an apparatus for making emulsions, such as emulsion paint.

clue.text: Continue with lawyer for hired criminal

blocks.note: go on means continue
DA is a US district attorney

explanation.surface: A lawyer continues to work for a hired criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goon' is temptingly close to the definition, but it comes from go on.
explanation.definitionFit: A goonda is a hired thug or ruffian in India, a criminal paid to intimidate.

clue.text: Instruments over-sentimental in recital

indicators.note: a recital is a spoken or performed delivery, so the word is heard

blocks.note: corny means mawkish or over-sentimental

explanation.surface: Instruments sounded mawkish at a concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recital' looks like a concert, keeping the musical picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Corni is the Italian plural of corno, horn, as written in orchestral scores, so musical instruments.

clue.text: See below river bank

indicators.note: in a down answer, below puts the first-named piece underneath the second

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for river
a see is a bishop's diocese, and Ely is one

explanation.surface: A note directing the reader to see below at the riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Below' places the see beneath the river in this down answer. 'See below' reads as a cross-reference; See is a diocese.
explanation.definitionFit: To bank on someone is to rely on them, so rely and bank are synonyms in that sense.

clue.text: Club member mostly fine

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the final letter is lost

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for member
an eric was a fine paid for murder in old Irish law

explanation.surface: A golf club member is mostly fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club member' reads as one unit, but 'Club' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A meri is a short flat Maori war club, made of stone or greenstone.

clue.text: Length of railway in Chicago?

blocks.note: first meaning: an old measure of cloth length
second meaning: Chicago's elevated railway is called the L, and this is the spelt-out name of that letter

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second meaning as a pun on the letter's name.
explanation.definitionFit: An ell is an old unit of length for cloth, and also the name of the letter by which Chicago's elevated railway is known.

clue.text: They show field strength over places no longer used

blocks.note: o'er is the poetic contraction of over
sted is an obsolete spelling of stead, a place

explanation.surface: Measurements of field strength taken over old abandoned sites.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No longer used' marks both pieces as archaic forms.
explanation.definitionFit: The oersted is a unit of magnetic field strength, named after the Danish physicist Hans Christian Ørsted.

clue.text: First-class large backing for brainy stuff

indicators.note: backing means moving in the opposite direction, so the letters are read from the end

blocks.note: A1 means first-class, written AI
LG is the abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: First-class backing for a large clever project.
explanation.walkthrough: AI + LG, all read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Glia are the supporting cells of the nervous system, tissue found throughout the brain, so brainy stuff is a playful definition.

clue.text: In Devon I clean bridge

blocks.note: che is the old Devon and Somerset dialect form of I
to valet a car is to clean it thoroughly

explanation.surface: Someone in Devon says they clean a bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: Devon is an English county in the south-west, whose old dialect said che for I, as used by Edgar in King Lear.
explanation.definitionFit: A chevalet is the bridge of a stringed instrument, the small piece supporting the strings.

clue.text: Stops fly inside combinations!

indicators.note: one thing inside another is placed within it

blocks.note: blocs are combinations of nations or parties
a kade, or ked, is a sheep tick, a wingless fly

explanation.surface: A fly is stopped inside one's long underwear!
explanation.walkthrough: Combinations are also a one-piece undergarment, which gives the surface its joke; here they are blocs.
explanation.definitionFit: To blockade is to seal off and stop movement in and out, so blockades means stops.
